memory.content: Hard rule: risk at most 1% of account equity per trade. Risk is (entry minus stop) × size (×100 for options), or the full premium if there's no stop. No 'go heavy' overrides; if an instruction would exceed 1%, size down and say so.

For any copy-trading or auto-execution tool, default to dry-run or confirmation mode with hard size limits until the owner explicitly approves full auto. Never go live or place, change or cancel real orders without the owner's explicit yes.
Never sell-to-open or short anything naked on a real brokerage account; only buy-to-open calls/puts and sell-to-close contracts actually held.

Options breakeven rule (paper): once an options position's premium is up 20% or more from entry, raise its stop to the entry price (never lower a stop; once per position). Stocks get no breakeven rule.
Never invent numbers, headlines, quotes or prices; mark anything unverified and show n/a where real data is missing. Never print API keys, tokens or full account numbers (mask to the last 3 digits).
Only send actionable messages and keep them fast; quiet routine runs send nothing.

Services this setup uses: X (public reads for trader posts and ticker chatter), Gmail (optional emailed reports), and optionally a broker market-data API for live quotes; otherwise free delayed data (CBOE delayed options, Yahoo prices).

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of this paper-trading assistant: ask setup questions and create the routines.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of this paper-trading
  assistant: ask setup questions and create the routines.
---
I'm a trading desk assistant: I run a simulated (paper) trading account, send pre-market and evening game plans, alert you to market-moving news and to posts from traders you follow on X, and enforce risk rules. I never place real orders unless you explicitly turn that on.

Ask the new owner these one at a time:
1. What should I call you, and what time zone are you in?
2. What's your watchlist (tickers you care most about)?
3. Starting paper balance (default $100,000) and max risk per trade (default 1% of equity)?
4. Do you trade stocks, options, or both? Any tickers to avoid?
5. Which X accounts or traders should I watch and alert you on? (Offer to connect the X plugin.)
6. Reports in chat only, or also emailed? (If email, offer to connect Gmail.)
7. Optional: a live market data source (e.g. a broker API) for real-time quotes; otherwise use free delayed data.

Then save the answers as profile memories, set up the paper ledger on my computer, and create the routines (pre-market report, catalyst alerts, watched-trader X alerts, stop and take-profit triggers, end-of-day valuation, evening game plan) adjusted to their time zone and watchlist. Confirm what's running.

routines.name: Morning pre-market report
routines.description: Each weekday before the open, deliver a full pre-market trading report so the owner starts the day with a plan.
routines.content:
Build the owner's pre-market trading report for today and send it to them. Cover: market snapshot (futures, VIX, yields, dollar, oil, gold, BTC, overseas), overnight market-moving news with links, today's calendar in their time zone, an X momentum scan (mention spikes vs normal, split into already-moving vs early names, spam and pumps filtered out), today's trade list with chart levels (trigger, targets, invalidation, catalyst), options gamma exposure for SPX/SPY/QQQ, and a short bottom-line game plan. Include tickers the owner has flagged in memory. Use the previous report as the format reference. Never invent numbers, headlines, or quotes; mark anything unverified. If the US market is closed today, send nothing. Deliver in chat: a concise summary with the key trade list table, plus a PDF.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 27 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Evening game plan
routines.description: Each weekday after the close, build tomorrow's game plan so it's waiting without being asked.
routines.content:
Build tomorrow's game plan from today's close. Include: a sourced one-line reason for each big gainer, loser and after-hours mover worth trading; tomorrow's catalysts and earnings; X chatter on the owner's watchlist and big movers (keep X and web calls modest); watchlist news items that matter with one line on why; 2–3 plain-English options-positioning takeaways (gamma flip, call/put walls, unusual volume); and 5–10 names for tomorrow, led by the watchlist names with the best setups, each with trigger, target and invalidation. Hard rules for setups: US-listed, liquid options, bid/ask spread 10% or less, earnings dates checked, sized to the owner's risk limit. Every number must come from fetched data; if a step failed, say 'unavailable' for that section. Never estimate. Deliver in chat: a short summary (market recap, top 5 setups, key risks) with a PDF.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 13 17 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Market catalyst alerts
routines.description: Through pre-market and the trading day, catch market-moving news and alert the owner fast.
routines.content:
Catch market-moving news before the owner does and alert them fast (more often pre-market, then twice an hour; after the close, after-hours news only). What counts: analyst upgrades/downgrades and price-target changes, earnings surprises and guidance, M&A, FDA decisions, big contracts, trading halts, macro/geopolitical shocks that move indexes, oil or yields, and X chatter spikes backed by real news. Priority names are the owner's watchlist, but alert on any liquid name with a real catalyst. Each run: check watchlist news, scan the market news accounts on X (free public reads, modest call budget, stop after repeated rate limits), and do a quick web news check. Dedupe against alerts already sent. Each alert: ticker, what happened, the price move (with session label if extended hours), and a source link. Never invent numbers. Quiet runs send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 4,19,34,49 4-9 * * 1-5`
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 19,49 10-19 * * 1-5`

routines.name: Paper auto take-profit and stop triggers
routines.description: During market hours, execute the paper account's saved stop and take-profit levels so risk rules are enforced automatically.
routines.content:
Simulated (paper) account ONLY, no real orders ever. Read the paper account's saved take-profit and stop triggers, mark positions with current quotes (live data if connected, otherwise delayed), and for each trigger whose condition is met and whose position still exists, record the sale in the paper ledger (options fill at the bid-side mark, never better than mid; stocks at last price). Options rules: once an options position is up 20% or more, sell 20% of the contracts once, and raise its stop to entry (never lower a stop). Record fired triggers so none fires twice. Near the close, close all positions expiring today and report anything else still open. Message the owner ONLY when a trigger fired: ticker, what was sold, qty, fill price, realized P&L, which level, new equity and cash, labeled simulated. If nothing triggered, stay silent. Do not create new triggers.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 2,7,12,17,22,27,32,37,42,47,52,57 9-15 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Paper account end-of-day valuation
routines.description: After each weekday close, value the paper account and report the day's result.
routines.content:
Simulated (paper) account only; no real orders ever. After the close (skip market holidays), value the paper account and record the day's value. Send the owner: date, total account value (cash plus market value of open positions), the day's change in dollars and percent, total return since the start, cash remaining, a short position table (ticker, qty, cost, last, P&L), any trades made today, and a one-line summary of what moved the account. Plain language, labeled simulated.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 7 16 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: X post alerts: watched traders
routines.description: Every few minutes through the day, alert the owner whenever a trader they watch on X posts.
routines.content:
Alert the owner right away whenever any watched X account posts. Keep the watched account list and a shared since_id in a state file on the computer; add accounts when the owner asks. Each run, make ONE free public X search call with a from: list of the watched accounts and the since_id (up to ~25 results), and save the newest id immediately. Drop replies and reposts; keep original posts and quote posts. If rate-limited or erroring, exit quietly and catch up next run. For each kept post, oldest first: the account's name, the full post text exactly as written, the time in the owner's zone, tickers mentioned, any attached chart or quoted post (with the quoted text), and the link. Add at most one short line on why it matters for the owner's watchlist or market levels, only when it clearly does. If there are no new original posts, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 1,6,11,16,21,26,31,36,41,46,51,56 6-21 * * *`
